title: How songwriters brought her material
summary: Writers brought songs such as "Sweet Georgia Brown", "Loveless Love" from Handy and Porter Grainger's numbers; she sang only what she felt.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yes. Now, tell me how did you, during those days, how did you get new material? Did song writers or people come to you?

Song writers would come to me, and in the meantime I wrote a whole lot of different songs myself. And a lot of those songs that Lovey had, I was in on them, but I didn't claim anything on them because she was so good about having my "Downhearted Blues" copy written and all, and was so honest about it, you know. And then I wasn't money crazy anyway. I just thought to make an honest living was the best thing to do, you know.

So in the meantime I would -- different -- oh, people would come in with songs. They would come in with songs. Macio Pinkert (PHONETIC) came in with "Sweet Georgia Brown," and Mr. Handy brought in -- what do you call it now -- "Careless Love". It was "Loveless Love". He brought in "Loveless Love".

I introduced it. I introduced it. Brought it on a piece of brown paper like you wrap groceries in, you know? And then Porter Granger, he came in with songs like "Michigan Water Tastes Like Sherry Wine," and Mike Jackson brought in songs to me. And, well, different ones, different people.
Let me see. Sissle and Blake? No, not Sissle and Blake. Different ones would, and somebody brought in a song to me called, "I'm Going Away Just to Wear You Off My Mind".
Which I made with Eubie Blake. Well, different ones would bring songs in to me, anyhow, and that's how I got my material.
If I liked them I would sing them. If I didn't feel them I wouldn't sing them. I didn't care. They
used to offer me money to sing them.
But I wouldn't sing them if I didn't feel them, because I wouldn't do it just for the money. It wasn't the money that I was too interested in. However, I wanted to make a living, see.
